title: The Brauer group of an arbitrary curve
statement:
Let $C$ be a curve over algebraically closed $k$ in the sense of
[def-sc-curves]; $C$ may be singular, non-reduced, disconnected or
have zero-dimensional components. Then its Brauer group ([def-br])
vanishes:

$$
H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf G_m)=0,
$$

with cohomology as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: Put C₀=C.nilradical.subscheme and i=C.nilradical.subschemeι. Mathlib gives reducedness and the closed immersion. Its range is the support of the nilradical, which is all of C; thus its closed embedding is a homeomorphism. Dimension is unchanged, and closed-immersion composition preserves the separated finite-type hypotheses, so i followed by f is a curve. Brauer pullback C → C₀ is injective.

Apply the existing finite smooth modification theorem to C₀: obtain Y, ν:Y→C₀, its separated finite-type structure morphism, dimension at most one, smoothness, finiteness, and a dense open V where ν is an isomorphism. Install these hypotheses as instances to construct IsCurve (ν≫i≫f). This is the component-normalization step of the original plan, including zero-dimensional and empty components.

The already proved smooth-curve theorem in this module, assembled from the smooth connected case by the clopen-component argument, gives Subsingleton Br(Y). Pullback along ν is injective by the finite-modification injection, so Function.Injective.subsingleton gives Subsingleton Br(C₀). Apply the reduction injection and Function.Injective.subsingleton again to get Subsingleton Br(C).
